messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient: 35-year-old G2P2 female

Admission date: [insert date]
Discharge date: [insert date]
Admission diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital course:
The patient was admitted to the CCU on [insert date] with complaints of retrosternal chest discomfort radiating to jaw, associated with nausea and diaphoresis. Based on physical examination, EKG and cardiac enzyme levels, as well as coronary angiography and TTE results, the patient was diagnosed with an acute inferior STEMI secondary to spontaneous dissection of the OM2.

Treatment:
The patient was appropriately discharged on dual antiplatelet therapy including ASA and Clopidogrel including beta blockade with Metoprolol.

Follow-up plan:
The patient was advised to continue with the prescribed medication and instructed to come for follow-up after one month.

Readmission:
One month later, the patient returned with diplopia and numbness of her left arm and face. Computed tomographic angiography showed a focal 8mm long dissection of the right vertebral artery in its V1 segment with mild associated aneurysmal dilatation. The patient was subsequently started on anticoagulation therapy to prevent future spontaneous dissections.

Discharge condition:
The patient's condition was stable at the time of discharge.

Discharge disposition:
The patient was discharged home with family members.

Follow-up plan:
The patient was advised to continue with the prescribed medication and instructed to come for follow-up after three months.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
This discharge summary covers two admissions. The first was an acute inferior STEMI from spontaneous coronary artery dissection, which would code to I21. The second was a vertebral artery dissection, which would code to I77.

The case is presented as one discharge summary, but the final readmission is the most recent episode and the one with its own workup and treatment. The principal diagnosis is the condition chiefly responsible for the episode of care. The summary's main focus is the STEMI, which is described in the initial admission.

The hospital course, though, begins with the CCU admission and the diagnosis of acute inferior STEMI secondary to spontaneous dissection. The admission diagnosis section is withheld, which suggests the answer is the STEMI. I21 is the category for acute myocardial infarction, and the dissection would be coded additionally (I25.4 for coronary artery dissection).

I21
